Subject: Private deployment telemetry — constraints and ask

Hi Tessa,

We’re kicking off the telemetry handoff for our Redwood private deployment (VPC + on-prem forwarder). A few constraints up front: our security team doesn’t allow arbitrary outbound internet; all egress must originate from an approved NAT/forwarder in the DMZ and go through the corporate proxy, and we require mutual TLS to customer-owned endpoints.

What we need from Redwood:
- A recommended egress pattern for logs/metrics/traces when the runtime is in private subnets (sidecar collector vs centralized DMZ forwarder).
- Concrete port/IP/host allowlist guidance and an example security-group / iptables snippet.
- Supported protocols and payload formats (syslog, Splunk HEC, OTLP/gRPC, Fluentd/Forward).
- Audit/evidence artifacts we can provide for SOC2 (e.g., verifier-friendly logs showing delivery, timestamps, sampling config).

Attached is our internal egress constraints doc for reference. Can we get a short architecture doc/runbook and a patch/example we can hand to infra? We’re aiming to complete network changes by Aug 28.

Thanks,

Alex — thanks for the clear requirements. Quick summary up front: two deployment patterns work well for constrained environments, and each has tradeoffs for latency, durability, and auditability. I attached a concise "telemetry cookbook" that maps requirements to implementation steps.

Recommended patterns (short):
1) Sidecar collector per node (preferred for minimal egress):
   - Each Redwood runtime runs a lightweight collector sidecar (OTel/Fluent Bit) that buffers to disk and forwards to an on-prem DMZ forwarder over mTLS (OTLP gRPC or Fluentd Forward).
   - Egress: single outbound destination (DMZ forwarder FQDN) on 443 (OTLP) or 24224 (Fluentd). Set up a NAT / proxy to restrict outbound hosts.
   - Pros: isolation, per-node buffering, simpler trace context propagation.

2) Centralized DMZ forwarder (preferred for strict egress controls):
   - Runtime -> VPC private-forwarder via internal LB -> DMZ forwarder (customer-hosted) -> SIEM.
   - Use mutual TLS between forwarder and SIEM; Redwood supports TLS client certs for forwarders.
   - Pros: single allowlist, simpler firewall policy, easier IP allowlisting for auditors.

Security & protocol notes:
- Supported endpoints: Splunk HEC (HTTPS), Syslog over TLS, OTLP/gRPC (TLS), Fluentd Forward (TLS).
- We recommend OTLP/gRPC for traces (ports 4317 or 443 proxied); traces should carry W3C traceparent so downstream can reconstruct spans.
- For metrics, push to Prometheus remote-write or metrics HEC depending on your SIEM.

Audit/evidence:
- We can produce: delivery receipts showing timestamps, per-route tokenized delivery IDs, and a compressed evidence bundle for SOC auditors. See cookbook section "evidence bundles" for expected artifacts.

Next steps I propose:
- I’ve attached a short cookbook with config snippets and sample security-group / iptables examples (telemetry-cookbook-v1.md).
- If you prefer, we can provide a small patch with OTEL collector configs (we can deliver a tracing-hook examples patch after call).
- Schedule a 30-minute runbook review (I’ll propose times below).

Attachments: telemetry-cookbook-v1.md
